title: Append-only archival pipeline for admin audit + tamper-evident proofs
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Build an append-only archival pipeline for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes that provides region-aware residency, configurable retention enforcement, and tamper-evident proofs. The goal is to provide a production-ready, auditable store that satisfies SOC/ISO-style evidence requirements without relying solely on third-party WORM vendors. This ticket covers schema extension, write-path guarantees, proof generation (Merkle tree or signing), residency routing, and the initial retention enforcement controller.
acceptance_criteria: All admin action, access, and config-change events are emitted to the archival pipeline with a stable schema version field
Append-only storage in customer region or customer-designated residency pool configurable per-org
Tamper-evidence mechanism implemented: signed manifests and periodic Merkle roots stored in an immutable anchor (object store + optional blockchain anchor)
Retention policy enforced by a controller that marks records for legal-hold and supports retention windows; deletion operations produce signed delete-requests recorded in an audit trail
End-to-end test demonstrating ingestion -> storage -> proof generation -> proof verification with synthetic data
Runbook updated, and initial performance impact on runtime write-path <5% at 99th percentile token throughput
work_log: 2026-02-11: Kickoff with PM (Lina Torres) and Security (Raj Patel). Agreed scope: admin actions + access + config changes for Private and Dedicated customers initially.

2026-02-18: Prototype of append-only writer implemented in runtime. Design decision: use append-only log file per region keyed by org-id to simplify residency. Trade-off: higher small-file count vs simplified per-org export and retention. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Append-Only+Archival+Design

2026-02-25: Security review (initial) - recommended HSM-signed root keys for proofs; decided to integrate with KMS first and add HSM option in later iteration. Action: ENG to add KMS key rotation support. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1987)

2026-03-03: Performance testing with synthetic event load (peak 12k rps). Observed 3.8% addition to p95 latency for write path when synchronous proof commit enabled. Decided to make proof commit asynchronous by default with configuration toggle for sync commit for high-assurance tenants.
2026-03-07: Migration plan drafted for existing audit exports (ENG-7321) to be replayed into new append-only format. Replay will run in a backfill job with sequence numbers to preserve ordering.

2026-03-10: Implementation of Merkle root calculator and signing flow completed. Proofs are stored as records with schema v2.0. Test harness for verification added: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools/tree/main/audit-proof

2026-03-12: Design review with PM and Legal. Legal requested retention-override and legal-hold flags per-customer. Added requirement: retention-controller must surface hold status via Console API and exportable CSV for eDiscovery.

Next steps: finalize retention-controller API, add residency policy routing to writer, add integration tests for KMS signing and proof verification, and start canary rollout to non-production Dedicated customers.
migration_plan: Phase 1: New writes go to append-only writer (feature flag).
Phase 2: Backfill historical audit exports via ordered replay jobs. Monitor for duplicate detection using event-id dedupe window.
Phase 3: Enable retention-controller for test tenants and run delete-simulations (no-op) to verify signed delete-records.
Phase 4: Canary enable proof verification in Console for selected tenants, then full rollout.
Rollback plan: feature flag off to stop writing new records; backfill paused; proofs remain verifiable for already-written segments.
testing_notes: Add unit tests for schema evolution (v1 -> v2) and backwards compatibility checks.
Integration test that verifies signature verification with KMS rotated keys (simulate rotation).
Chaos test: simulate partial write failures and verify idempotent replay behavior and observable alerts in Console.
Load test with residency sharding to ensure write amplification is acceptable.
e2e: Demonstrate evidence package generation (zip of records + proof manifest) exportable for auditors.
